title: Enhanced Third-Harmonic Generation in Diamond Photonic Crystal Slabs via Doubly Resonant Quasi-Bound States in the Continuum
authors: Sangmin Ji, Satoshi Iwamoto, Hideki Gotoh
abstract: We propose and numerically demonstrate doubly resonant third-harmonic generation (THG) in a diamond photonic crystal (PhC) slab, in which the fundamental harmonic (FH) and the third harmonic (TH) modes are simultaneously resonant within the same membrane. A hexagonal-lattice slab with triangular air holes is designed so that a K-point band-edge FH mode and a $Γ$-point quasi-bound-state-in-the-continuum (quasi-BIC) TH mode satisfy the frequency-tripling condition $3ω_1\approxω_3$. Modifying the hole shape from circular to equilateral triangular breaks the in-plane symmetry that otherwise forces the nonlinear coupling to vanish, thereby converting a TH mode with negligible overlap into one with finite while simultaneously reducing the required slab thickness. Guided by a closed-form expression for THG efficiency derived from coupled-mode theory, we design the unit cell and a PhC heterostructure cavity. Three-dimensional simulations of the designed cavity yield a normalized THG efficiency $η=2.7\times10^{-7}~\mathrm{W}^{-2}$ under moderate quality factors, which is projected to reach ~$0.034~\mathrm{W}^{-2}$ at the fabrication-limited quality factor (Q = 200,000). Because the operating wavelength is set by the lattice constant, this design, combined with the ultra-wide transparency window of diamond, can map a single geometry across various fabricable wavelengths, spanning from telecommunication bands to color-center-resonant visible and deep-UV outputs. These results establish a robust route toward efficient, monolithic on-chip frequency conversion in an all-diamond platform for quantum and nonlinear photonics.
summary: The paper presents a design for enhancing Third-Harmonic Generation (THG) using a Photonic Crystal cavity embedded in diamond. By engineering the lattice structure to create doubly resonant quasi-bound states at both the fundamental and third harmonic frequencies, they overcome symmetry limitations that typically suppress nonlinear coupling. The resulting device promises highly efficient, monolithic on-chip frequency conversion applicable across multiple wavelengths.
main_problem: The core problem is achieving efficient, monolithic on-chip frequency conversion, specifically Third-Harmonic Generation (THG), within a centrosymmetric material like diamond for quantum and nonlinear photonics.
main_result: The authors designed a photonic crystal heterostructure cavity that achieves a high projected THG efficiency ($\sim 0.034 	ext{ W}^{-2}$ at $Q=200,000$), establishing a robust route for on-chip frequency conversion across various wavelengths.
method: The study uses coupled-mode theory and 3D Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) simulations to model the THG process in a doubly resonant cavity.
model_or_system: The system is a diamond Photonic Crystal (PhC) slab with a hexagonal lattice containing triangular air holes. It is engineered as a heterostructure cavity designed to support simultaneous resonance for the Fundamental Harmonic ($\omega$) and the Third Harmonic ($3\omega$).
key_observables: Normalized THG efficiency ($\eta$), Quality Factors ($Q_1, Q_3$), and the nonlinear overlap integral ($ eta_3$).
important_parameters: The frequency tripling condition ($3\omega \approx \omega_3$) must be met; high quality factors ($Q \sim 200,000$) are crucial for enhancement.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that breaking the in-plane symmetry by using triangular holes is necessary to activate a non-zero nonlinear coupling ($ eta_3$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures (showing FH and TH modes), optimization plots of the Figure of Merit ($Q_3| eta_3|^2$), and 3D field distributions for both fundamental and third harmonic fields in the optimized cavity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the theoretical framework using coupled-mode theory, detailing the design strategy involving symmetry breaking (circular to triangular holes) to activate nonlinear coupling, optimizing the heterostructure parameters ($n_{core}, n_{trans}, n_{clad}$), and finally presenting high-Q simulation results demonstrating superior THG performance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it demonstrates advanced photonics engineering—using photonic band structure control (BICs) in a solid-state platform like diamond—to enhance nonlinear optical processes, which is a key area of quantum optics and cavity QED research.
